errors.english: Even though I was shaken, I did not let go.
errors.why: What was stirring is the harmer (anger) that the speaker did not let loose, not the speaker being shaken; the same misreading recurs in the king's question.

errors.english: When it is born, one becomes unmanifest [note: meaning one loses their noble character or clarity],
errors.why: When anger arises the good is not seen, in parallel with the next line (when it has not arisen the good is evident); the note invents a different sense.

errors.english:
When it arises in men who wish for harm,
They feel a certain joy;
errors.why: The anger arises in oneself and those who wish one ill rejoice at it; it does not arise in the ill-wishers.

fix.find:
When it arises in men who wish for harm,
They feel a certain joy;
fix.replace:
Whenever it arises [in one],
Those who wish one ill rejoice;

errors.english: But one is said to have abandoned it [note: referring to a false accusation of losing one's temper], then bad reputation arises,
errors.why: The verse says ill repute comes to the one in whom heart-burning anger is (not abandoned), fading like moonlight at dawn; the note's false-accusation scenario is not in the text.

note: The narrative frame is sound, but the verses on anger have one clear case-role error and two muddled verses with speculative notes.

errors.english: is nothing other than a non-ascertainment
errors.why: The Tibetan is a double negative: that ascertainment is certainly not a non-ascertainment, i.e. it is genuine, which is the objector's point answered next.

note: A careful rendering of a dense commentary on the avayavin; the argument structure is followed well.

errors.english: otherwise, there would never be any actual purpose at all
errors.why: The point is that otherwise the thing would not be occasional (occurring only sometimes); དོན here is the thing, not a purpose.

errors.english: If Indra's forehead has the nature of fire,
errors.why: Śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head', is the name of the anthill in the PV I.36 example, so a reader needs that sense, and 'forehead' obscures it.

note: The causal-nature argument and the summary verses are rendered accurately, apart from the anthill example and one misread clause.

errors.why: This line, which completes སྦྱིན་ from the previous side, says 'making clear the excellence of giving'; 'for the benefit of others' replaces it.

errors.english: is born into the world of the Sugata One Gone to Bliss
errors.why: བདེ་བར་འགྲོ་བ here (Skt. prakaṭitasugatiḥ) describes the jewel among men as one whose good destiny is manifest, and he is born in this world, not into 'the world of the Sugata'.

note: The colophon and the Śāketa description are sound, but the closing verse line and the opening ornate verse are misconstrued.
Both the Sanskrit and the Tibetan verse lines are translated faithfully and kept parallel.

errors.english: when it is said that it is pervaded by one portion of the direction of the property of the (subject) dharmin that is to be proven
errors.why: ཕྱོགས here is pakṣa (thesis), as in PV I.1 pakṣadharmas tadaṃśena vyāptaḥ: the property of the subject to be proven is pervaded by a part of the pakṣa.

fix.find: when it is said that it is pervaded by one portion of the direction of the property of the (subject) dharmin that is to be proven
fix.replace: when it is said that the property of the (subject) dharmin that is to be proven is pervaded by one portion of the thesis (pakṣa)

errors.why: The reason is that existence in all instances is impossible for a particular, not that a distinction is impossible.

errors.english: In order to understand the pervader, it is appropriate to understand the qualified itself.
errors.why: The qualified/pervaded is what makes the pervader known (gamaka) and the pervader is what is made known; the English makes the qualified the object of understanding.

note: The overall shape of the vyāpti discussion survives, but pakṣa is mistranslated as 'direction' and the gamaka/gamya relation is inverted.

errors.english: made them establish residences for him
errors.why: གནས་འཆའ་བ is the Vinaya act of taking formal dependence (niśraya) on a teacher: Udāyin had the novices take dependence on him.

fix.find: made them establish residences for him
fix.replace: had them take dependence (niśraya) on him

errors.english: Except for those that do not produce filth
errors.why: With སྲོག་ཆགས་ from the previous side, it means except those in which living creatures have not arisen; 'filth' is not in the text.

errors.english: bundles of grass should be spread out, tied with ropes, and left suspended from trees
errors.why: The bundles meant for spreading on the walkway are to be kept tied with rope and hung on trees until they are spread, not spread and then hung.

errors.english: Materials for cleaning such as dung
errors.why: འདག་རྫས is plaster or floor-daubing material, and the dung is its ingredient, not a cleaning agent.

note: The Udāyin narrative is readable, but a key Vinaya term (taking niśraya) and several practical rules in the walkway passage are misrendered.

errors.english: The engagement of the mind apprehending an entity produces an incompatible cause in the form of a latent impression, which the mind apprehending a non-entity then interrupts.
errors.why: The cognition of non-entity is the one that produces the opposing cause (a vāsanā) and thereby cuts off the continuum of the cognition of entity.

note: The argument about mutual exclusion of concepts is followed, though the 'blue' overextension sentence is garbled and one key agent is reversed.
A faithful rendering of the word-by-word gloss on the tigress episode.

errors.english: refers to not distributing the robes of the monastic community
errors.why: In context (washing, dyeing, bowl-work and wood-splitting) བགོ means 'wear': one does not wear the Saṃgha's robe at those times.

fix.find: refers to not distributing the robes of the monastic community
fix.replace: refers to not wearing the robe belonging to the monastic community

errors.english: Where a father, mother, brother, or sister openly gives from their own home
errors.why: The giver is the insane person, giving from his own home in the presence of his father, mother or siblings, as the next clause (where they are not present) shows.

note: The Vinaya-sūtra commentary is mostly followed, but the opening misreads 'wear' as 'distribute' and the madman case confuses who gives.
